name: Fatima El-Sayed
headline: Founder at Relaykit; former product manager at Brightline Pay
statement: Relaykit builds approval-gated agents for small lenders. Raising a pre-seed round and looking for a security-minded engineer who can take us to Kubernetes before a SOC 2 review.
summary: Second-time founder building agents for back-office finance teams; strong on product, thin on infrastructure.
building: Relaykit, agents that reconcile ledgers for small lenders under human sign-off.

project.description: Relaykit lets back-office teams at small lenders hand reconciliation and exception handling to an agent that proposes journal entries and waits for a human to approve. We have two design partners on a pilot. The agent runs as a single Python process on one VM with the OpenAI key in an env file, and the partners' auditors are starting to ask who the agent is, what it may touch, and how we prove what it did. We need to pass a SOC 2 readiness review by January and we have no one on the team who has run production infrastructure.
project.summary: An approval-gated reconciliation agent for small lenders that needs production infrastructure and an audit story before SOC 2 readiness.
pain_points: no workload identity or scoped credentials for the agent
no tamper-evident audit trail of agent actions
single VM deployment with secrets in an env file
SOC 2 readiness with nobody who has done it
pilot partners asking compliance questions the team cannot answer
connection_ideas: A security engineer who has given workloads SPIFFE or similar identities and can scope what the agent may call.
A platform engineer who has taken a single-VM service to Kubernetes with secrets management.
Someone who has been through a SOC 2 audit at a fintech and knows which controls auditors actually test.
A payments engineer who understands double-entry ledgers and can sanity-check the journal entry model.

name: Björn Karlsson
headline: Site reliability engineer at Lumen Grid, multi-tenant Kubernetes
statement: Looking for people who have hardened multi-tenant clusters and anyone doing per-tenant chargeback.
summary: Keeps one cluster serving a dozen internal teams without them noticing each other; fluent in network policy and blame-free postmortems.
building: Tenant cost and noisy-neighbour dashboards for shared clusters.

project.description: We are opening our internal multi-tenant cluster to two external partners next quarter. Today tenants are separated by namespaces and network policy, and every team gets the same quotas. Partners want proof that their workloads cannot see each other's traffic or secrets, finance wants a per-tenant bill, and I want to stop hand-editing quotas. I have the Flux layout and the dashboards; what I do not have is a convincing threat model or a way to generate the per-tenant cost report without a spreadsheet.
project.summary: Hardening and metering a shared Kubernetes cluster before external partners are onboarded.
pain_points: no written threat model for cross-tenant isolation
per-tenant cost report is a spreadsheet
partners will ask for compliance evidence
connection_ideas: A security engineer who has threat-modelled multi-tenant clusters and can poke holes in the network policy story.
A FinOps person who has built per-tenant chargeback from Prometheus or billing exports.
Someone who has written admission policies with OPA or Kyverno for quota enforcement.

name: Samuel Adeyemi
headline: Independent full-stack engineer; previously at Pebble Studio

summary: Freelance full-stack engineer who ships small products fast and keeps getting pulled back into invoicing problems.
building: An invoicing and collections tool for freelancers in West Africa.

project.description: Freelancers in Lagos and Accra invoice clients in three currencies and chase payment over WhatsApp. I built a working invoicing tool with 120 users, but payouts still go through a manual bank transfer, FX is whatever the bank says that day, and the onboarding screens were designed by me at 2am. I want to add card and mobile-money collection, settle in the freelancer's currency, and get a designer to look at the flow before I spend money on ads.
project.summary: A multi-currency invoicing tool for West African freelancers that needs payment rails, FX handling and design help.
pain_points: no FX strategy beyond the bank's daily rate
no marketing plan beyond word of mouth
card and mobile-money collection not integrated
connection_ideas: A payments engineer who has built a multi-currency ledger and knows where FX rounding bites.
A product designer who will review the onboarding flow and point at the three worst screens.
A growth marketer who has launched a product to freelancers or small businesses.
Another builder serving freelancers, to compare notes on acquisition.
